description.narrative: The project is implemented in South Africa. The main outcome areas it contributes to are peace and dialogue. The main rights holders are marginalised people (LGBTQIA, women, disabled, youth, migrants). Through social dialogue and provision of high-quality information and analytic insight the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between SALO and the Palme Center. The Southern African Liaison Office (SALO) is a South African-based civil society organisation which contributes to building peace and security through facilitating dialogue and consensus between national, regional and international actors. Focused predominantly on Southern Africa, especially Zimbabwe and Swaziland.Other Donors to the Organisationo European Union Delegation to South Africa o Irish Embassy o Open Society Initiative for Southern Africa (OSISA) o The Norwegian Embassy o Norwegian Peoples Aid SA o Norwegian Peoples Aid OSLO o The Netherlands Embassy o FES o Ford Foundation o The Royal Danish Embassy The Palme Center will organise a donors meeting with Norwegian Poples Aid, FES and OSISA in order to clarify which components and activities are funded by whom in order to complement each other rather than overlap, but also to make it easier for SALO when reporting.Project ObjectiveDemands from CSOs from Zimbabwe and Eswatini to South Africa-based policy makers are reflected in policy pronouncements and there is growing consensus among stakeholders on the need for action that counters P&amp,S issues in respective countries. Women, women movements, LGTBQI persons and other marginalised groups are more empowered to fight for their rights and against discrimination. South African Government/ANC alliance make more input into human security and rights situation in project countries as well as South Africa itself. Push for dialogue and concrete action built through informed consensus.Actor groupsDecision makers: South African government (SAG), particularly the DOJ and its Deputy Minister, COGTA, Department of Women, DIRCO in general and Gender Desk at DIRCO, Home Affairs, COGTA, Social Development, ANC, ANC International Relations Committee, COSATU and NEHAWU. Actor working in cooperation: PASSOP, the Zimbabwe Solidarity Forum, Action for Conflict Transformation, the Solidarity Peace Trust, the Crisis in Zimbabwe Coalition, specialist refugee and xenophobia organisations like CORMSA, and academic institutions including University of Pretoria, WITS University, UJ, UCT and UNISA. Rightsholders: Marginalised people (LGBTQIA, women, disabled, youth, migrants)
